description: The figure contains two vertically stacked bar charts titled “mBERT” (top) and “XLM-R” (bottom) that illustrate percent-point differences by model layer, with each bar representing the value for a specific layer index and an additional “concat” condition. In both panels, the category axis is the horizontal axis: in the mBERT chart it is labeled with layer indices 0 through 12 plus a final unlabeled tick corresponding to the rightmost bar, while in the XLM-R chart it is explicitly labeled “layer” and shows ticks 0 through 12 followed by “concat”; the categories are arranged in increasing layer order from left to right. The value axis is the vertical axis labeled “% point difference,” shown on a linear scale with tick marks at 0, −2, −4, −6, −8, and −10, spanning roughly from about 0 down to about −11. In the mBERT panel, all bars are a light blue color; approximate values by layer are: 0 ≈ −10.5, 1 ≈ −8.6, 2 ≈ −7.6, 3 ≈ −5.1, 4 ≈ −3.9, 5 ≈ −2.5, 6 ≈ −0.8, 7 ≈ −0.8, 8 ≈ −0.3, 9 ≈ 0.0, 10 ≈ 0.0, 11 ≈ −0.2, 12 ≈ −1.3, and the rightmost bar (final tick) ≈ +0.3. In the XLM-R panel, all bars are a darker blue; approximate values are: 0 ≈ −9.6, 1 ≈ −9.6, 2 ≈ −8.2, 3 ≈ −5.8, 4 ≈ −3.5, 5 ≈ −2.2, 6 ≈ −0.6, 7 ≈ −0.5, 8 ≈ −0.6, 9 ≈ −0.4, 10 ≈ +0.3, 11 ≈ +0.4, 12 ≈ −0.3, and “concat” ≈ +0.4. The bars are not visually stacked or grouped beyond being separate single-series bars per category, and there are no legends, annotations, or special highlighting beyond the distinct color used for each model panel.
